messages:
tanya: heads-up SFO edge p99 jumped ~200-400ms starting ~03:12 UTC. throughput dip and tail spikes. KV cache hitrate fell 92% -> 54% around the same time. @neil @chen can you take a look?
ops-bot: alert: sfo-pop latency_spike detected (p99 350ms, error-rate +0.7%)
neil: any recent deploys or batching config changes? or a noisy tenant?
tanya: no deploys. autoscaler steady. batching heuristics look same but avg CPU/time-per-token nudged up. attaching a quick profiler snapshot: https://redwood-storage/internal/snapshots/2178456789/prof.html
chen: quick skim of the flamegraph — attention kernel time spikes align with KV eviction bursts. looks like kvcache churn -> more recompute. possible noisy-tenant prefix churn.
samir: can someone grep kernel_selector logs for 03:10-03:20? I want to see if there were rapid kernel flips.
tanya: pasted a snippet from host10 logs: `kernel_choice: attn_fast_v2 -> attn_fallback_q8 (latency_delta=45ms)` repeated ~every 7s for the same model shard.
marta: that's interesting — selector oscillation can cause KV layouts to be incompatible across runs, causing cold misses. net logs show a short burst of retransmits on host10 around 03:12 too.
neil: selector oscillation + network jitter + a noisy container could explain simultaneous KV misses and CPU spikes. can we check cgroup/steal?
tanya: cgroup dump shows one container (noisy-tenant-192) had CPU steal jump 3x at 03:11-03:13. I throttled it and moved affinity.
perf-bot: perf counters: host10: context-switches +56%, L3-misses +42% during window. kernel_selector_flip_rate spiked to 12/min.
chen: mitigation suggestion: pin attention kernel to `attn_fallback_q8` on affected hosts and increase kvcache TTL for SFO route to 60s while we root-cause.
samir: rolling kernel-pin to host10,host11,host12 now. command used:```
./admin/kernel_pin --hosts host10 host11 host12 --kernel attn_fallback_q8
```
samir: monitoring — host11/12 p99 back near baseline within 90s, host10 improving after cgroup tweak but still noisy.
tanya: great work. next steps: postmortem + reproduce test in staging simulating CPU steal + network jitter to validate selector stability and KV warmup. I'll open INC-217845 follow-up.
marta: +1. also adding an alert: `kernel_selector_flip_rate > 5/min` for SFO and other edge pops. :thumbsup:
ops-bot: incident auto-resolved — p99 restored at 03:35 UTC. Incident record: INC-217845.
notes: Investigation tied kernel selector oscillation to noisy tenant CPU steal and network jitter causing KV cache churn; short-term mitigations: kernel pinning and kvcache TTL bump; follow-up: repro test and alert for flip rate.
